messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: Batch sorption isotherms and short-contact-time tests were performed for multiple PFAS using the same contaminated groundwater and both PAC and GAC (WEB04-E01, WEB04-E02, WEB04-E04), which reasonably supports a judgment of comparability with conditions.
WEB04-E01 states that batch sorption isotherms were measured, and WEB04-E02–E03 report Freundlich coefficients and n values; this clearly indicates a sorption endpoint.
WEB04-E04 reports 20–40% removal with GAC and 60–90% removal with PAC in short (10-minute) contact time tests, which is a removal/adsorption-performance endpoint rather than degradation.
WEB04-E01 explicitly states that the tests used contaminated groundwater from a PFAS-impacted well, matching the matrix description.
WEB04-E01 notes use of both powdered and granular activated carbon; specifying powdered activated carbon (PAC) as the sorbent form is directly supported for the subset of interest.
No unit is appropriate for sorbent_form, and none is given; the text (WEB04-E01) only specifies material types, not a quantitative unit.
WEB04-E04 states that short (10-minute) contact time tests were conducted, matching the value of 10 for contact_time.
WEB04-E04 specifies a 10-minute contact time; use of the unit "min" is correct.

WEB04-E01 describes batch sorption isotherms, and WEB04-E02–E03 report Freundlich parameters (log K_iF and n), supporting the characterization as batch sorption isotherms modeled with a Freundlich isotherm.
No unit applies to a qualitative test-type descriptor, so a null unit is appropriate and not contradicted by WEB04-E01–E03.
WEB04-E02 explicitly mentions PFOS and its Freundlich coefficient, supporting inclusion of perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS).
WEB04-E02 explicitly mentions PFOA and its Freundlich coefficient, supporting inclusion of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA).
WEB04-E01 states that batch sorption isotherms were measured for three perfluorosulfonates; this matches the description, which does not name them individually.

WEB04-E01 states that batch sorption isotherms were measured for five perfluoroacetic acids; this matches the record’s description of five perfluoroacetic acids/perfluoroalkyl carboxylates without individual names.

WEB04-E02 reports that for PFOS, log K_iF was "about 4.0" for PAC. The recorded value 4.0 matches numerically but is labeled as exact_numeric rather than approximate, so the magnitude is supported but the precision qualifier is overstated.
WEB04-E02 reports dimensionless Freundlich log K_iF values; leaving the unit null is appropriate.
WEB04-E02 reports that for PFOA, log K_iF was "about 3.8" for PAC. The recorded value 3.8 matches numerically but is treated as exact_numeric, whereas the source indicates an approximate value.
WEB04-E02 describes log K_iF as a dimensionless Freundlich coefficient; a null unit is appropriate.
WEB04-E03 states that Freundlich n values were generally around 0.5; the recorded value "~0.5" with approximate_numeric form accurately reflects this.
Freundlich n is a dimensionless exponent; leaving the unit null is appropriate and consistent with WEB04-E03.
WEB04-E04 reports 60–90% removal with PAC in 10-minute contact time tests; the recorded range 60–90 matches this statement.
WEB04-E04 expresses removal as a percentage; the unit "%" is correct.

WEB04-E01 indicates that all tests used contaminated groundwater from a single PFAS-impacted well. From this design fact, it necessarily follows that results may not generalize to other water chemistries, supporting a design_inferred limitation about matrix generalizability.

The statement that the abstract does not report PAC dose, pH, or co-constituent concentrations is about missing information. The cited locators (WEB04-E01 and WEB04-E04) do not themselves state or logically require that these details are absent; absence from the provided snippets alone is not a sufficient basis under the rules, so this design_inferred limitation is not supported at the cited grain.

WEB04-E01 describes batch sorption isotherms and WEB04-E04 describes short contact-time tests with activated carbon in contaminated groundwater, supporting bench-type experimental work. However, the term "bench-scale" and the emphasis solely on PAC (omitting that GAC was also used) are interpretive qualifiers not explicitly stated in the cited text.

WEB04-E01 notes use of powdered and granular activated carbon; WEB04-E02 and E04 explicitly give PAC-specific performance. Describing the treatment as powdered activated carbon (PAC) adsorption is supported for the subset of interest, even though GAC is also studied in the paper.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—study identity, matrix, treatment (PAC adsorption), endpoint types (sorption and removal), and key quantitative findings (Freundlich coefficients, n, and % removal)—are all supported by the cited abstract text. The only issues are minor qualifier precision on approximate values and one unsupported limitation about unreported conditions, which do not compromise use of the quantitative adsorption data for synthesis.
